hypothesis: Who the household is (demographics) and when the snapshot is (calendar) predict 4-week spend.
transformation_description: Baseline: demographic codes, has_demographics, snapshot day index, week-of-year.

hypothesis: A household's recent purchasing behavior — trailing-window spend, trip frequency, recency and spend rate — predicts its next-4-week spend far better than demographics alone.
transformation_description: Added RFM features: spend/trips/days in windows 28/56/84/112/182/365d, recency, tenure, basket size, spend rates, trend, discount share, store count.
reasoning_summary: Future spend is strongly autocorrelated; recent spend and trip frequency are the classic best predictors of near-term grocery spend.

hypothesis: What a household buys (department spend mix, private-brand share, department breadth, store concentration) predicts its 4-week future spend beyond RFM.
transformation_description: E001 RFM + demographics + department spend shares, brand shares, n_depts_28d, store HHI (56d).
reasoning_summary: Category-mix captures stable household preferences that modulate future spend level; brand share and breadth reflect engagement style.

hypothesis: Marketing exposure and engagement predict future spend: campaign targeting (TypeA/B/C counts, active campaigns, days since first target) and coupon redemption activity (counts in windows, recency, redemption rate per campaign) plus shopping time-of-day habits and discount-usage shares.
transformation_description: E002 + marketing features: campaign target counts by type, active campaign count, days since campaign start, coupon redemptions in 28/84/182/365d windows, redemption recency, redemption rate, time-of-day habits, coupon/retail discount share of spend.
reasoning_summary: Campaign targeting and coupon redemption are direct signals of retailer engagement that should correlate with future spend; time-of-day and discount habits add behavioral texture beyond E002's product-mix features.

hypothesis: Future 4-week spend repeats seasonal/level patterns: spend in the same 4-week window one year earlier, the household's typical (exponentially decayed) 28-day block spend, and its recent trend predict future_spend_4w beyond trailing-window RFM.
transformation_description: E002 + 13 non-overlapping 28d block spends, seasonal lag spend/trips (lags 364/392/336d), all-time avg 28d spend, decayed block mean/sum, 6-block trend slope, zero-block count, dispersion, and spend ratios.
reasoning_summary: Trailing 28d spend is a noisy proxy for usual monthly spend; a decayed block mean and same-window-last-year spend capture the household's stable level and seasonality, which should predict the next 28 days better.

hypothesis: Spend dynamics — recency-decayed spend, short-window spend/trips, weekly level/volatility/trend, zero-spend streaks, inter-purchase gaps, deal-seeking, day-of-week and time-of-day habits, variety and unit-price — carry predictive signal beyond E004's static window sums and seasonal lags.
transformation_description: E004 + 37 dynamics features: EWMA spend (halflife 14/28/56/112d), 7/14d spend+trips, weekly spend mean/std/active-weeks and OLS slopes (12/24w), trailing zero-week streak, inter-purchase gap mean/std/max (84d), deal shares and discount amount, day-of-week spend shares (182d), shopping-hour mean/std, product variety/units/unit-price, 28d-block max/std.
reasoning_summary: E004 uses coarse window sums; dynamics capture momentum, regularity and recency decay that should sharpen near-term spend predictions, especially for active households.

hypothesis: Future 4-week spend largely repeats the household's own staple products: a per-product cadence forecast (expected 28d spend per product, decayed by days since last purchase) plus product-concentration and repeat-purchase-share features capture structure that household-level RFM aggregates miss.
transformation_description: E006 + 15 product-cadence features: top-10-product expected spend (all-time avg 28d per product, recency-decayed), staple spend shares/momentum, days-since-last stats, product HHI & count, repeat-purchase share.
reasoning_summary: Spend is concentrated in a household's repeated staple items; forecasting at the product level with recency decay should beat pure household-level aggregates, which E006 already saturates.

hypothesis: Momentum and purchase rhythm predict future 4-week spend: recent-vs-prior spend/trip ratios, weekly trend slope, dormancy gaps and trip regularity, discount engagement, timing concentration, unit-price level, and upcoming campaign targeting carry signal beyond the level features in E006.
transformation_description: E006 + 25 momentum/rhythm features: spend & trip momentum ratios (28d vs prior 28/56d), weekly spend slope (linear + log over 8w), gap mean/std/max/cv, idle-day fraction, days since 2nd-last trip, trip regularity CV (84d), discount amount/ratio/line-share (28/84d), days since coupon redemption, day-of-week & trans_time concentration, unit price, line counts, and count of campaign targets starting in the next 28d.
reasoning_summary: E006's level features (spend windows, EWMAs) may miss whether spend is accelerating or decelerating and whether the household is regular or dormant; momentum and rhythm features should sharpen both the high-spend tail and the zero/low-spend predictions.

hypothesis: The target is heavy-tailed and zero-inflated; the fixed model fits multiplicative structure better when spend/trip/recency features are log-transformed, and the household's activity state (inactive 28d, returning after a gap, very low trip count) plus volatility/level ratios (block CV, EWMA ratio, recency/gap) carry predictive signal that raw-scale features miss.
transformation_description: E006 + 22 features: log1p of spend (7/28/56/84/182/365d), trips (28/84/182d), recency, tenure, mean gap, EWMA-28; booleans inactive-28d/56d, returning-after-gap, low-trips-28d; block CV, EWMA14/EWMA112 ratio, recency/gap ratio, log-spend × log-tenure interactions.
reasoning_summary: Tree/linear models on raw dollar scales under-weight low-spend and zero-spend households; log features compress the tail and state flags let the model treat churned/returning households separately, which should cut MAE given the zero-inflated target.

hypothesis: The fixed model over-predicts lapsed households: ~21% of targets are exactly 0 and a simple rule (predict 0 when trailing-28d spend < $5) cuts MAE by 1.3 in my LOSO proxy. Linear spend levels can't express this; capped/hinge spend features (spend_28 split at $5, EWMA split at $5/$25, recency hinge at 28d), a lapsed indicator, activity-probability EWMA and spend×activity interaction let the model shrink small predictions and capture nonlinearity. Also prune E006's 147 features to the 45 most permutation-important to reduce noise.
transformation_description: E006 pruned to 45 permutation-ranked features + 10 new: sp28_lo/sp28_hi (spend_28 split at $5), ew28_lo/ew28_hi (EWMA-hl28 split at $5), rec_lo/rec_hi (recency hinge at 28d), lapsed flag, act_ewma28, act_share_26w, exp_spend (spend_28 × act_ewma28).
reasoning_summary: Residual analysis shows the model over-predicts near-zero targets; hinge/capped spend features plus activity-probability features let a linear model express the zero-rule that alone was worth ~1.3 MAE, while pruning removes noise features.

hypothesis: Shopping style and purchase regularity predict future 4-week spend: basket value/size, unit price tier, deal reliance, store repertoire, trip timing and day-of-week mix, inter-trip gap structure, and historical zero-spend block rate carry signal beyond window-sum RFM.
transformation_description: E006 + 26 style/regularity features (84d basket stats, unit price, discount ratio, store count/top-store share, dow spend shares, morning/evening shares, gap mean/std/max over 365d, zero-28d-block rate over 364d).
reasoning_summary: E006 captured how much households buy but not how they shop; style traits (premium vs value, deal-driven, store-loyal, regular vs erratic cadence, churn-prone) should stabilize level predictions and improve low/zero-spend calibration.

hypothesis: Absolute department-level spend composition (top-12 departments + shares) in trailing 28d/84d windows, plus department spend in the same 4-week block one year earlier, predicts future 4-week spend beyond totals and style features.
transformation_description: E012 + 51 new department-mix features: spend by top-12 department groups (GROCERY, DRUG GM, MEAT, PRODUCE, KIOSK-GAS, MEAT-PCKGD, DELI, PASTRY, MISC, NUTRITION, SEAFOOD-PCKGD, FLORAL) + OTHER in trailing 28d and 84d windows, 28d department shares, and same-block-1-year-ago (day-363..-336) department spends.
reasoning_summary: Department mix captures what the household buys, which is more stable than totals and drives future category spend; the 1-year seasonal block adds category seasonality the calendar features can't express.

hypothesis: Finer-grained recency structure — weekly spend buckets over the last 8 weeks, finer EWMA half-lives (7/21/42/84d), weekly CV and lag-1 autocorrelation, and big-trip concentration — carries predictive signal for future 4-week spend beyond coarse 28/84-day aggregates.
transformation_description: Replaced E012's features with 21 new recency/regularity features computed from raw transactions (weekly buckets w1..w8, EWMA hl 7/21/42/84, EWMA trips hl28, weekly mean/CV/autocorr, big-trip max/count/top1-share).
reasoning_summary: E012 uses coarse windows; a finer recency grid may track level shifts better. This standalone table tests the new features' signal strength before combining them with the E012 core (which must be rebuilt from scratch since saved tables cannot be loaded inside build_features).

hypothesis: A leave-one-snapshot-out ridge blend of all 173 E012 features, fit in log space, provides a denoised level estimate that the fixed model can exploit as a single strong feature.
transformation_description: E012 + 2 stack features: stack_ridge_log (LOSO ridge on log1p target, alpha=300, oof on train rows) and stack_ridge (expm1).
reasoning_summary: The fixed model has struggled to combine 173 correlated features; a regularized cross-fitted blend compresses them into a robust level signal and may lift accuracy beyond the 62.43 plateau.

hypothesis: The 7,492 validation rows missing from E012's feature table (build_features computed no features for them) can be filled by a vectorized raw-transaction pipeline; adding those rows plus extra raw recency features (weekly-spend stats, department 28d spends) improves MAE.
transformation_description: E012 features + rawrec extras (sp56/84/182/365, tr84/182, q28, ew, wk28, wkm/wks/wkmx/wkmn/wkm2, 44 dept 28d spends) merged on household_key+snapshot_day; validation rows now complete.
reasoning_summary: E012's table was missing 7,492 validation rows entirely; a vectorized cumsum pipeline fills them and adds raw weekly/dept recency features.

hypothesis: Leak-free peer-outcome kNN features — the median realized next-28d spend of the 25/50 most similar households in the same cohort whose outcome is already known — capture a nonparametric, self-calibrating spend level that the ridge stack misses, especially for heavy spenders it currently under-predicts.
transformation_description: E015 + 4 leak-free peer-kNN features (knn_med25/50, knn_mean50, knn_medlog50) computed per snapshot from a same-cohort reference pool (tenure≥84d) matched on log current-window spend/trips, recency, tenure, prior-window spend; self excluded.
reasoning_summary: Standalone peer-median already beats the stack OOF at train snapshots (69.9 vs 74.0 at d=431) and a 50/50 blend cuts MAE ~7 points there; as extra columns the fixed model can learn the optimal blend itself.

hypothesis: The fixed model's MAE-optimal predictor is best fit in sqrt-target space (which balances the heavy tail) and as a 75/25 blend of sqrt² and raw-space LOSO ridge fits; replacing E015's log-space stack features with leak-free sqrt/raw stack features lowers validation MAE below 62.2.
transformation_description: Replaced the two log-space stack features with four leak-free stack features: LOSO ridge (α=300, winsorized 221-col E012 feature matrix) fit on sqrt(target) with square back-transform, on raw target, their 75/25 blend, plus the raw sqrt fit; validation rows get full-train fits.
reasoning_summary: OOF analysis showed sqrt-space ridge beats log-space ridge by ~7 MAE points and a 75/25 sqrt²/raw blend beats either alone (62.75 vs 62.9-64.4), so the same stack construction should transfer to the validation snapshots.
